alerts.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 29 at 10:53AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
ESFGJT

Low pressure begins to dig southward from the PACNW on Friday,
tapping into a fetch of Pacific moisture that will evolve into an
atmospheric river streaming into the Desert Southwest this weekend.
Showers and thunderstorms develop on Friday and Saturday across the
region. Lighter rainfall totals Friday and Saturday will reflect,
initially lower, moisture. However, a few thunderstorms could produce
impactful downpours on saturated soils left over from last weekend's
historic rainfall.

Deeper moisture develops Saturday night and early Sunday. This is
expected to produce heavier and more widespread rainfall across
southeast UT and southwest CO Sunday and Monday, mostly below 10000
feet. While rivers are forecast to remain below action stage, a
growing concern lies in the potential for runoff around saturated
hillsides in the region. This could produce rock, mud, and debris
flows onto roadways, as well as flash flood prone burn scars, washes,
slot canyons, and arroyos. Early estimates predict an area of 1 to 2
inches of new rainfall for portions of southeast UT and southwest CO.

This is a preliminary forecast that hinges on slight shifts in a
strong moisture plume impacting the region. It also attempts to
capture the most statistically likely outcome, despite stronger and
weaker outlier predictions. Outdoor enthusiasts, motorists, and
residents of recent flood impacted areas are encouraged to remain
abreast of the developing forecast in the coming days.

alerts.title: Paving Operations-150324
alerts.description: Between Frontage Road and County Road 232 (near Durango) from Mile Point 88 to Mile Point 89.5. Paving operations. Starting October 29, 2026 at 7:00PM MDT until October 30, 2026 at about 7:00AM MDT. Full schedule below: • October 29, 7:00PM - October 30, 7:00AM Comment: The US 550-US 160 Grandview Interchange exit and entrance ramps will experience staggered nighttime closures from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., Sunday night through Friday morning. Motorists traveling southbound and northbound on US 550 between Durango and New Mexico will detour on Wilson Gulch Drive and Three Springs Boulevard to access the Grandview Bridge and points beyond. For more information email: resurfacingproject@gmail.com.

alerts.title: US 160 Pagosa Springs Reconstruction-147604
alerts.description: Between US 84 and Pike Drive (Pagosa Springs) from Mile Point 144.3 to Mile Point 141.8. Road construction. Starting October 29, 2026 at 7:00AM MDT until October 29, 2026 at about 6:00PM MDT. Full schedule below: • October 29, 7:00AM - October 29, 6:00PM Comment: Harman Park & Piedra Road-Work is underway at this intersection of US 160. Working hours will be intermittent day and night so motorists should plan for potential delays, Monday-Saturday. Please allow extra time to get through the work zone. Safety benefits of this work includes pedestrian safety upgrades and ADA accessibility improvements. Expect lane shifts and up to 15-minute delays. Crews will switch two-way traffic into the eastbound lanes, perform temporary striping operations and begin asphalt milling in the westbound lanes. Parking will not be permitted on US 160 and vehicles will be towed at the owner's expense. Westbound lane closures, 10’ width and 75’ length restrictions will remain in place 24/7 through end of 2026. Work is weather-dependent. For questions contact the project team at 970-335-9230 or Pagosa160reconstruction@gmail.com Project Webpage: www.codot.gov/projects/us160pagosasprings
